t: A chiefdom joins several villages under a hereditary paramount chief who rules through kinship, ritual and tribute, without the officials, standing army or written law of a state.
Chiefdoms arose independently in Mesopotamia, Europe, the Americas, Africa and Polynesia, and some, like Cahokia and the Hawaiian chiefdoms, raised great monuments and fed large followings.
Anthropologists named the type in the 1950s and still argue over it, while chiefs remain a recognised tier of local government from Sierra Leone and Botswana to Samoa.
dyk: The word cacique, which Spanish conquerors applied to native rulers throughout the Americas, was borrowed from the Taíno, whose chiefdoms Columbus met in the Caribbean in 1492.
ev: Temple towns of the Ubaid period rise in southern Mesopotamia; many archaeologists see them as early chiefdoms
A few richly furnished graves on Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast reveal one of Europe’s first hereditary elites
Cahokia, near present-day St Louis, grows rapidly into the largest chiefly centre north of Mexico
Columbus reaches the Taíno chiefdoms of the Caribbean; Spanish conquest destroys them within a generation
Hernando de Soto’s expedition passes through Cofitachequi and Coosa, paramount chiefdoms of the South-East
English colonists at Jamestown meet Wahunsenacawh, paramount chief of some thirty peoples of Tidewater Virginia
Kamehameha I conquers Oʻahu at the Battle of Nuʻuanu; by 1810 he rules all the Hawaiian Islands
Kalervo Oberg names the chiefdom as a type; Elman Service sets it between tribe and state in 1962

f.power: A paramount chief from the senior line of a ranked descent group, above lesser chiefs who ruled villages or districts and passed tribute upward
f.legitimacy: Descent from founding ancestors or gods, rites that only chiefs could perform, success in war, and generosity in feasts and gifts
f.chosen: Inherited within the chiefly lineage, usually by seniority of descent, but often contested among close kin and settled by councils or by war
f.examples: Cahokia (c. 1050–1350), the Hawaiian chiefdoms before Kamehameha I, the Taíno chiefdoms of Hispaniola, the Powhatan paramount chiefdom, the Natchez under the Great Sun
